newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses hit by sharp Wall St drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses hit by sharp Wall St drop.

text.p: European bourses fell on Friday, depressed by Wall Street which tumbled one percent at the opening as fresh U.S. economic data added to fears of higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average lost more than 50 points at Friday's start after Commerce Department figures showed new orders received by U.S. factories climbed strongly during July.

The dollar drifted slightly lower against the mark but foreign exchange trading was expected to be quiet as U.S. dealers made an early start to the Labor Day weekend. The focus remained on the French franc.

London, Frankfurt and Paris all registered losses when New York plunged at the opening after closing overnight 1.13 percent down overnight. It was down 55.11 points at 5592.54 within minutes of the start on Friday.
Investors' fears of higher U.S. interest rates were rekindled when the healthy factory orders were added to Thursday's strong growth data.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped 18.5 points to 3,866.5 on the FTSE 100 share index. The drop followed a nearly one percent fall on Thursday in a London market that has been hitting new peaks recently, culminating in a record FTSE close on Wednesday.
Markets were have turned jittery over the the economic data emerging from Washington over the last few days -- and more is coming next week

Investors will be anxiously awaiting the important U.S. employment report for August due to be published next Friday. Strong figures, taken with today's data, could be the impetus for the U.S. central bank to increase interest rates in coming weeks, an unwelcome prospect for equity markets. In Frankfurt, stocks on the computerised IBIS index fell 0.7 percent amid gloom about the U.S. data. Floor trading ended earlier, down 0.63 percent
French stocks fell 0.52 percent at midafternoon after shedding 1.27 percent on Thursday on worries about the prospect of industrial unrest in the autumn.
The CAC-40 index slipped 10.05 points to 1,967.51 and the franc strengthened to 3.4222 against the mark after hitting a five-month low of 3.4296 against the German currency on Thursday.
A drop of 20,000 in French July unemployment, announced on Friday, and a continuing trade surplus in June, albeit slightly reduced from May, gave some comfort to investors.
The dollar, which perked up on Thursday on the U.S. growth figures, was slightly weaker, at 1.4782 marks, as the mark continued to strengthen against most European currencies.

Analysts were at a loss to explain the dollar's weakness, which defies the textbooks since it should be rising on expectations of monetary tightening as higher U.S. rates would make assets denominated in dollars relatively more attractive.
"The dollar's reaction to strong economic data is schizophrenic but it remains vulnerable to upset in the asset markets," said Ian Amstad, international economist at Bankers Trust in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 108.60 yen and 1.4782 marks, compared with 108.50 and 1.4815 in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 18.5 at 3,866.5.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended down 16.23 points at 2543.83.
The Paris CAC-40 was down 12.07 at 1,965.49.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $386.45 in the afternoon, compared with Thursday's close of $388.25. Silver was at $5.17, down five cents.
